q: What is the chemical symbol for Gold?
exp: Gold's chemical symbol is Au, from the Latin 'Aurum'.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall common chemical symbols
• Gold = Au
• Silver = Ag
• Sodium = Na
• Potassium = K

Step 2: Understand the origin
• Gold's symbol comes from Latin 'Aurum'
• Silver's symbol comes from Latin 'Argentum'

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Go): Not a valid chemical symbol ✗
• Option B (Gd): Gadolinium, a different element ✗
• Option C (Au): Gold (from Aurum) ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Ag): Silver (from Argentum) ✗

The correct answer is C) Au.

q: The atomic number of an element is determined by the number of:
exp: Atomic number equals the number of protons.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define atomic number (Z)
• Atomic number = Number of PROTONS in nucleus

Step 2: Distinguish related terms
• Mass number (A) = Protons + Neutrons
• Electrons = Protons (in neutral atom)
• Nucleons = Protons + Neutrons

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Neutrons): Determines isotopes, not atomic number ✗
• Option B (Protons): Defines the element, = atomic number ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Electrons): Equals protons in neutral atoms ✗
• Option D (Nucleons): Total particles = mass number ✗

The correct answer is B) Protons.

q: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
exp: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall atmospheric composition
• Nitrogen (N₂): 78.08% ← MOST ABUNDANT
• Oxygen (O₂): 20.95%
• Argon (Ar): 0.93%
• Carbon Dioxide (CO₂): 0.04%
• Others: Trace amounts

Step 2: Analyze options
• Option A (Oxygen): Second most (21%) ✗
• Option B (CO₂): Only 0.04% ✗
• Option C (Nitrogen): 78%, most abundant ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Hydrogen): Trace amounts only ✗

The correct answer is C) Nitrogen.

q: The pH of pure water at 25°C is:
exp: Pure water is neutral with pH 7.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall the pH scale
• 0-6: Acidic
• 7: Neutral
• 8-14: Basic/Alkaline

Step 2: Understand pure water
• At 25°C, [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³
• pH = -log[H⁺] = -log(10⁻⁷) = 7

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (0): Strongly acidic ✗
• Option B (5): Acidic ✗
• Option C (7): Neutral ✓ Correct!
• Option D (14): Strongly basic ✗

The correct answer is C) 7.

q: Which of the following is a noble gas?
exp: Argon is a noble gas in Group 18.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall noble gases (Group 18)
• Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), Radon (Rn)

Step 2: Understand noble gas properties
• Full outer electron shell
• Unreactive/inert

Step 3: Classify options
• Option A (Oxygen): Group 16, reactive ✗
• Option B (Nitrogen): Group 15, reactive ✗
• Option C (Argon): Group 18, noble gas ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Chlorine): Group 17, halogen, reactive ✗

The correct answer is C) Argon.

q: The chemical formula for water is:
exp: Water is H₂O - two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall water's composition
• 2 Hydrogen atoms + 1 Oxygen atom
• Chemical formula: H₂O

Step 2: Analyze each option
• CO₂: Carbon dioxide (1 C + 2 O) ✗
• H₂O: Water (2 H + 1 O) ✓
• O₂: Oxygen gas (2 O atoms) ✗
• NaCl: Sodium chloride/salt ✗

Step 3: Verify
• H₂O has: 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen = water ✓

Option A: Carbon dioxide ✗
Option B: Water ✓ Correct!
Option C: Oxygen gas ✗
Option D: Salt ✗

The correct answer is B) H₂O.

q: Which bond type involves the sharing of electrons?
exp: Covalent bonds form when atoms share electrons.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall bond types
• Ionic: TRANSFER of electrons (metal + non-metal)
• Covalent: SHARING of electrons (non-metal + non-metal)
• Metallic: Sea of delocalized electrons
• Hydrogen: Weak intermolecular attraction

Step 2: Match the description
• "Sharing of electrons" = Covalent bond

Step 3: Examples
• Covalent: H₂O, CO₂, CH₄, O₂
• Ionic: NaCl, MgO

Option A: Electron transfer ✗
Option B: Electron sharing ✓ Correct!
Option C: Electron sea ✗
Option D: Weak force ✗

The correct answer is B) Covalent bond.

q: The molar mass of oxygen gas (O₂) is approximately:
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Calculation:

Step 1: Recall atomic mass of oxygen
• Oxygen (O) = 16 g/mol

Step 2: Identify O₂ structure
• O₂ = 2 oxygen atoms bonded together

Step 3: Calculate molar mass
• Molar mass = 2 × 16 = 32 g/mol

Step 4: Analyze options
• Option A (16): One oxygen atom only ✗
• Option B (32): 2 × 16 = 32 ✓ Correct!
• Option C (8): Half an atom ✗
• Option D (64): 4 oxygen atoms ✗

The correct answer is B) 32 g/mol.

q: Which indicator turns red in acidic solution?
exp: Methyl orange turns red in acidic solutions.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall indicator colors in acid
• Litmus: RED in acid, blue in base
• Phenolphthalein: COLORLESS in acid, pink in base
• Methyl orange: RED in acid, yellow in base
• Universal: Multiple colors (red/orange/yellow/green/blue/purple)

Step 2: Identify the specific indicator
• Question asks for one that turns RED in acid
• Methyl orange specifically turns red

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Litmus): Also red, but methyl orange is the classic answer for this exact question
• Option B: Colorless in acid ✗
• Option C (Methyl orange): Red in acid ✓ Correct!
• Option D: Multiple colors ✗

The correct answer is C) Methyl orange.

q: The chemical symbol for Sodium is:
exp: Sodium's symbol is Na, from Latin 'Natrium'.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall element symbols and origins
• Sodium = Na (from Latin 'Natrium')
• Sulfur = S
• Potassium = K (from Latin 'Kalium')

Step 2: Analyze options
• Option A (S): Sulfur, not sodium ✗
• Option B (So): Not a valid symbol ✗
• Option C (Na): Sodium (Natrium) ✓ Correct!
• Option D (K): Potassium (Kalium) ✗

Step 3: Memory aid
• Na in sodium comes from 'Natrium'
• K in potassium comes from 'Kalium'

The correct answer is C) Na.
